examples.ko: 왕이 화가 나서 신하를 탑에 감금했어요.
examples.en: The king got angry and confined his official in a tower.
Confining a person is a serious crime.
In the movie, the villain locks the hero in a basement.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 죄인을 감금하고 재판을 기다리게 했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, they confined offenders and made them wait for trial.

examples.ko: 어떤 이유로도 사람을 감금하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never confine a person, whatever the reason.
I saw a news story about a case of holding someone captive.

explain: '가두다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '감금하다'는 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 사람을 억지로 가둘 때 써요. 동물이나 물건에는 보통 '가두다'를 써요. 반대로 풀어 줄 때는 '풀어 주다'나 '석방하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '가두다' is the everyday word; '감금하다' shows up in news and legal contexts when a person is locked up against their will. For animals or objects people usually say '가두다'. The opposite is '풀어 주다' or '석방하다'.

examples.ko: 이 버스는 시청을 경유해서 공항에 가요.
examples.en: This bus goes to the airport via City Hall.
I flew from Incheon to New York by way of Tokyo.

examples.ko: 홍콩을 경유하는 비행기 표가 더 싸요.
examples.en: The flight ticket with a stopover in Hong Kong is cheaper.

examples.ko: 부산에 갈 때 대전을 경유할 거예요.
examples.en: I will go through Daejeon on my way to Busan.
Where did you stop over on the way back?

examples.ko: 이 길은 시장을 경유하고 학교로 이어져요.
examples.en: This road passes through the market and leads to the school.

explain: 버스나 비행기 안내에서 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '거쳐서 가다'가 더 자연스러워요. 거치는 곳 앞에는 '을/를'을 붙이고, '경유'는 자동차 연료 이름이기도 해요.
explain_en: You hear it a lot in bus and flight announcements. In casual speech '거쳐서 가다' sounds more natural. The place you pass through takes '을/를', and '경유' is also the word for diesel fuel.

examples.en: In court, the lawyer defended his client.

examples.ko: 친구가 잘못했을 때도 저는 늘 친구를 변호해요.
examples.en: Even when my friend is in the wrong, I always stand up for them.
Nobody spoke up for him.

examples.ko: 억울한 사람을 변호하고 싶어서 법대에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to law school because I wanted to defend wronged people.

examples.ko: 동생을 변호하는 엄마의 말에 형이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: The older brother got angry at his mother's words defending the younger one.
Who will speak up for me?

explain: 법정에서 변호사가 하는 일에도 쓰고, 일상에서 누군가의 편을 들어 말해 줄 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '편들다', '감싸 주다'가 더 가벼운 말이에요. '~을/를 변호하다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: It describes a lawyer's work in court, and also speaking up on someone's side in daily life. In everyday talk '편들다' and '감싸 주다' are lighter. It takes the pattern '~을/를 변호하다'.

examples.en: I assembled a desk with my dad on the weekend.
I look at the manual and put the chair together.
This toy is hard to assemble by yourself.

examples.ko: 부품을 다 조립하면 전원을 켜 보세요.
examples.en: When you have assembled all the parts, turn on the power.
I built my computer myself and use it.
I work assembling cars at a factory.

explain: 가구, 장난감, 컴퓨터처럼 여러 부품을 맞춰 만드는 물건에 써요. 반대말은 '분해하다'예요. 작은 것을 끼워 맞출 때는 '맞추다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it for things made of several parts, like furniture, toys, or computers. The opposite is '분해하다'. For fitting small pieces together, '맞추다' is also common.

examples.en: Critics gave this movie favorable reviews.
Many people praise the new app.

examples.ko: 그 식당을 호평하는 글이 인터넷에 많아요.
examples.en: There are many posts online praising that restaurant.
I read an article that praised the book and bought it.
My teacher spoke highly of my presentation.
The customers praised the taste of the food and left.

explain: 평가하는 사람이 주어일 때 '호평하다'를 써요. 평가를 받는 쪽에서는 '호평을 받다'라고 해요. 반대말은 '혹평하다'예요.
explain_en: Use '호평하다' when the person giving the review is the subject. From the side being reviewed, say '호평을 받다'. The opposite is '혹평하다'.

examples.ko: 시민들이 정부의 결정에 규탄 성명을 냈어요.
examples.en: Citizens issued a statement condemning the government's decision.

examples.ko: 폭력 사건 이후 규탄의 목소리가 커졌어요.
examples.en: After the violent incident, voices of condemnation grew louder.
That remark drew condemnation from society.

examples.ko: 학생들이 학교 앞에서 규탄 집회를 열었어요.
examples.en: Students held a protest rally in front of the school.
Condemnation of the company continued in the newspapers.

examples.ko: 거리에서 규탄 구호를 외치는 사람들이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see people shouting slogans of protest in the street.

explain: 뉴스나 시위에서 주로 쓰는 공식적이고 센 표현이에요. 일상에서는 '비난'이나 '욕'이 더 흔해요. 보통 '규탄 집회', '규탄 성명', '규탄을 받다'처럼 짝을 지어 써요.
explain_en: A formal, strong word you mostly meet in news and protests. In daily life '비난' or '욕' is more common. It usually appears in set pairs like '규탄 집회', '규탄 성명', and '규탄을 받다'.

examples.en: Citizens strongly condemned the violence.
Many people condemn this incident.
I sent a letter to the newspaper denouncing the wrongdoing.

examples.ko: 모두가 그의 거짓말을 규탄하고 사과를 요구했어요.
examples.en: Everyone denounced his lie and demanded an apology.
Let's try to sort it out by talking rather than denouncing in the streets.
The government condemned the assault and promised an investigation.

explain: 공개적으로 강하게 잘못을 따질 때 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 가볍게 말할 때는 '비난하다', '욕하다'를 써요. '비판하다'보다 훨씬 센 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means publicly and forcefully calling out a wrong, so it is rarely used in casual talk. For lighter situations people say '비난하다' or '욕하다'. It feels much stronger than '비판하다'.

examples.ko: 그의 말은 곧 떠난다는 걸 암시했어요.
examples.en: His words hinted that he was leaving soon.
The first scene of the movie foreshadows the ending.

examples.ko: 하늘이 어두워지는 건 비가 올 것을 암시하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The darkening sky seems to hint that rain is coming.

examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 문제를 슬쩍 암시해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher gave us a quiet hint about the exam questions.

examples.ko: 그 표정은 뭔가 숨기고 있음을 암시하고 있어요.
examples.en: That expression suggests he is hiding something.

examples.ko: 저는 거절할 때 직접 말하지 않고 암시하기도 해요.
examples.en: Sometimes I hint instead of saying no directly.

explain: '힌트를 주다'는 일상적인 말이고, '암시하다'는 분명히 말하지 않고 넌지시 보여 줄 때 써요. 사람의 말이나 사건이 앞으로 일어날 일을 미리 알려 줄 때도 써요. 명사 '암시'는 '암시를 주다', '암시를 받다'로 써요.
explain_en: '힌트를 주다' is the everyday phrase; '암시하다' is for suggesting something without saying it outright. A person's words or an event can also hint at what will happen. The noun '암시' goes with '암시를 주다' and '암시를 받다'.

examples.en: He was caught while forging a passport.
Counterfeiting money is a serious crime.
He forged documents and deceived the company.
Someone forged my signature.
The person who forged and sold tickets was arrested.
If you forge a painting, you will be punished by law.

explain: 돈, 서류, 도장, 그림처럼 진짜인 척하는 가짜를 만들 때 써요. 법적인 문제로 이어지는 느낌이 강해요. 비슷한 '변조하다'는 진짜를 몰래 고치는 것이고, '위조하다'는 처음부터 가짜를 만드는 거예요.
explain_en: Use it for making a fake that passes as real, such as money, documents, seals, or paintings. It carries a strong legal tone. '변조하다' means secretly altering a real thing, while '위조하다' means making a fake from scratch.

en: practice moderation; restrain oneself; (medical) cut out

examples.en: I cut back on sweet food for my health.
Even when you are angry, you have to keep your emotions in check.
He is a person who watches his words.

examples.ko: 돈 쓰는 걸 절제하니까 저금이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since I held back on spending, my savings grew.

examples.ko: 다이어트 중이라 많이 먹는 걸 절제하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm on a diet, so I'm holding back on eating a lot.

examples.ko: 슬픈 장면에서도 감정을 절제한 연기가 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: The restrained acting, even in the sad scene, was impressive.

explain: 먹는 것, 돈, 감정, 말처럼 지나치지 않게 스스로 조절할 때 써요. '참다'는 하고 싶은 걸 견디는 것이고, '절제하다'는 평소에 알맞은 선에서 멈추는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '자제하다'가 있어요. 의학에서 병든 부분을 잘라 내는 '절제(切除)하다'도 있는데, 한자가 달라서 소리만 같은 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: Use it for keeping food, money, emotions, or words from going too far. '참다' is enduring something you want to do, while '절제하다' feels like habitually stopping at a reasonable point. A similar word is '자제하다'. In medicine there is also '절제(切除)하다', to surgically cut out a diseased part; its Chinese characters differ, so it is a different word that only sounds the same.

examples.ko: 새 다리를 올해 말에 준공할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The new bridge is scheduled to be completed at the end of this year.
The company completed construction of a new factory.

examples.ko: 시청이 새 도서관을 준공해서 시민들이 기뻐해요.
examples.en: City Hall finished building the new library, and citizens are happy.

examples.ko: 건물을 준공하려면 안전 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To complete a building, you must pass a safety inspection.

examples.ko: 아파트를 준공하고 나서 바로 입주가 시작됐어요.
examples.en: Move-in began right after the apartment complex was completed.

examples.ko: 터널을 준공하는 날에 큰 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: A big event is held on the day the tunnel is completed.

explain: 건물, 다리, 도로 같은 큰 공사가 끝났을 때 써요. 작은 일에는 안 쓰고 '끝내다', '마치다'를 써요. 공사를 시작하는 건 '착공하다'예요. 뉴스에서는 '준공식', '준공 검사'로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when a large construction project, like a building, bridge, or road, is finished. For small things say '끝내다' or '마치다'. Starting construction is '착공하다'. In the news it also appears as '준공식' and '준공 검사'.

examples.en: Even after hearing the explanation, it is hard to be convinced.

examples.ko: 저는 그 결과를 납득할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't accept that result.
Once I gave the reason, everyone was convinced.
My mom accepted my choice too.

examples.ko: 납득하지 못한 사람은 손을 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please raise your hand if you are not convinced.
Sign only after you fully understand and agree.

explain: '이해하다'는 내용을 알아듣는 것이고, '납득하다'는 알고 나서 '그럴 만하다'고 받아들이는 거예요. 그래서 '납득이 안 가요', '납득할 수 없어요'처럼 부정형으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: '이해하다' is about grasping the content, while '납득하다' is accepting it as reasonable once you understand. That is why it often appears in negative forms like '납득이 안 가요' and '납득할 수 없어요'.

examples.en: My teacher strongly stressed the importance of reading every day.
The doctor stresses strongly that exercise is absolutely necessary.

examples.ko: 그는 환경을 지키자고 역설하며 연설을 마쳤어요.
examples.en: He ended his speech arguing strongly that we protect the environment.
No matter how strongly I argued, people didn't listen.

examples.ko: 대표가 새 계획의 필요성을 역설한 뒤 회의가 끝났어요.
examples.en: The meeting ended after the CEO stressed the need for the new plan.
She wrote a book that argues strongly for freedom.

explain: '강조하다'보다 더 힘주어, 자기 생각이 옳다고 설득하듯 말할 때 써요. 연설, 강연, 글 같은 공식적인 자리에서 주로 써요. 명사 '역설'에는 '모순처럼 들리지만 맞는 말'이라는 다른 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '강조하다' and sounds like persuading others that your view is right. It is used mostly in formal settings like speeches, lectures, and writing. The noun '역설' also has another meaning, a paradox.

examples.ko: 할머니가 저에게 김치 담그는 법을 전수해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother passed down to me how to make kimchi.
The master craftsman passed his skills on to his apprentice.
I don't hand this secret down to just anyone.
He passed his know-how to his juniors and retired.
There is a school that teaches and preserves traditional dance.
I'm worried because there is nobody to pass the skill on to.

explain: 기술, 비법, 전통처럼 오래 쌓인 것을 한 사람이 다른 사람에게 직접 가르쳐 물려줄 때 써요. 일반 지식을 가르칠 때는 '가르치다'를 써요. '기술 전수', '비법 전수'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when one person directly teaches and hands down long-built things like skills, secret recipes, or traditions. For ordinary knowledge, use '가르치다'. It also appears as a noun in '기술 전수' and '비법 전수'.

examples.en: The war began with an invasion by the enemy country.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 외국의 침공에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned about foreign invasions in history class.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 여러 번 침공을 당했어요.
examples.en: That country was invaded many times.
People were shocked by the news of the invasion.
An alien invasion of Earth is the plot of the movie.
After the invasion, the city collapsed completely.

explain: 전쟁과 역사 이야기에서 주로 써요. '침공을 받다/당하다', '침공하다'로 쓰고, 비슷한 '침략'은 땅이나 나라를 빼앗는 데 초점이 있어요. 영화에서는 외계인 '침공'처럼 가볍게도 써요.
explain_en: Mostly used in stories about war and history. It appears as '침공을 받다/당하다' and '침공하다', and the similar '침략' focuses on seizing land or a country. In films it is also used lightly, as in an alien '침공'.

examples.en: We compromised with each other on the price.
Both sides give in a little and reach a compromise.
I never compromise on quality.
In the end, we decided to meet in the middle.
The couple settled on a moving date and signed the contract.

examples.ko: 쉽게 타협하면 나중에 후회할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you compromise too easily, you may regret it later.

explain: 서로 조금씩 양보해서 합의에 이를 때 써요. 비슷한 '합의하다'는 결과에, '타협하다'는 서로 물러서는 과정에 초점이 있어요. 원칙을 쉽게 버리는 느낌이 있어서 '타협하지 않다'는 자기 기준을 지킨다는 칭찬이 되기도 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 하고 싶던 일을 접고 형편에 맞게 선택한다는 뜻이에요. 조금 씁쓸한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means giving up what you really wanted and choosing what fits your circumstances, with a slightly bitter feeling.

explain_en: Use it when both sides give a little and reach agreement. '합의하다' focuses on the result, while '타협하다' focuses on the process of both sides backing off. It can feel like dropping principles too easily, so '타협하지 않다' can be praise for holding your standards.

examples.en: The navy fleet entered the port.
In the movie, the space fleet protected the Earth.

examples.ko: 이순신 장군의 함대는 바다에서 크게 이겼어요.
examples.en: General Yi Sun-sin's fleet won a great victory at sea.

examples.ko: 배 열 척으로 이루어진 함대를 만들었어요.
examples.en: They built a fleet made up of ten ships.
I saw a model of an old fleet at the museum.
The fleet commander gave the order to set sail.

explain: 역사 이야기나 전쟁·우주 영화에서 자주 나와요. 배가 많이 모여 있어도 군함이 아니면 보통 '선단'이라고 해요. '우주 함대'처럼 상상 속 이야기에도 써요.
explain_en: It comes up often in history and in war or space movies. A group of many ships that are not warships is usually called '선단'. It is also used in imagined stories, as in '우주 함대'.
